label: dataset structure
text: DATA FACT: The file 159007346.node is an h5ad with 19259 nuclei x 32227 genes, no layers (so raw counts are in X, which holds integer-valued counts), obs columns sample/total_counts/n_genes/age_group/n_genes_raw, and sample has 3 levels (3M=Adult 11518 nuclei; 21M1 and 21M2=Aged), so batch=sample and sample is fully nested in age_group.

label: use uncorrected log1p CP10K for means
text: PITFALL: Expression summaries computed from integrated/batch-corrected values (Seurat integrated assay, corrected embeddings or rescaled data) are distorted, and Seurat recommends using the original uncorrected data for expression. CHECK: Confirm that the Edn1 means come from log1p(CP10K) of raw X after the n_genes>1000 filter, not from scaled, regressed or integrated values; integration should only feed PCA/kNN/clustering. IF FOUND: Recompute the per-type means from log1p(normalize_total(target_sum=1e4)) of raw counts. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/discussions/4000

label: sample confounded with age
text: PITFALL: Batch (sample) is fully confounded with age_group (3M Adult vs 21M1/21M2 Aged), so integration can over-correct or leave sample-specific clusters, and an age-specific vascular state could split off and be mislabeled. CHECK: After clustering, cross-tabulate cluster x sample; flag clusters that are more than 90% from one sample, and check that each major label contains nuclei from all 3 samples. IF FOUND: Label sample-specific clusters by their markers anyway (do not drop them), and confirm that the winning cell type is the same when means are computed per sample. SOURCE: https://divingintogeneticsandgenomics.com/learn/guides/integration-overcorrection-in-scrna-seq/ ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/4785

label: RPCA substitute in python
text: PITFALL: Scanpy has no native Seurat RPCA, so teams will substitute Harmony, Scanorama or an omicverse/trackcell RPCA port, and the choice can change cluster boundaries for small populations (endothelial, mural, immune). CHECK: Record which integration was used; rerun clustering with a second method (or none) and see whether the major-label assignment of the vascular, fibroblast and SGC clusters stays the same. IF FOUND: If the top cell type changes between integration methods, report the instability and prefer the most RPCA-faithful port (omicverse rpca_integrate / Seurat RPCA via R). SOURCE: https://github.com/omicverse/omicverse/pull/899 ; https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v4.3/integration_rpca

label: ambient RNA misannotation
text: PITFALL: In DRG/brain snRNA-seq, ambient RNA (mostly from high-UMI neurons) contaminates all glial and non-neuronal nuclei, which can give clusters spurious marker expression and cause misannotation. CHECK: For each cluster, inspect mean expression of every marker panel (not only the top one); a cluster that is positive for neuronal Isl1/Prph at low levels together with strong glial or vascular markers is likely contaminated glia, not neurons. Also check whether Edn1 is broadly low-level across all clusters (ambient) or concentrated in one. IF FOUND: Assign the label by the dominant, specific marker panel (relative to other clusters), not by the presence of any neuronal marker. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/neuron/fulltext/S0896-6273(22)00815-7 ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-023-02978-x

label: vascular doublets/mixed clusters
text: PITFALL: Endothelial-mural (pericyte) and endothelial-fibroblast heterotypic doublets or contaminated nuclei form small clusters co-expressing Pecam1/Flt1 with Rgs5/Notch3 or Col1a1/Pdgfra, so endothelial transcripts leak into a mural or fibroblast label (or vice versa); at resolution 0.6, endothelial and mural nuclei may even share one cluster. CHECK: For the clusters labeled Endothelial, Mural and Fibroblast, compute mean Pecam1, Flt1, Rgs5, Notch3, Col1a1 and Pdgfra and the fraction of nuclei co-expressing panels; check the n_genes/total_counts of mixed clusters (doublets are higher). IF FOUND: Label a mixed cluster by its dominant panel, but test the robustness of the ranking by excluding the mixed cluster or sub-clustering it; if a single vascular cluster mixes EC and mural, sub-cluster it before assigning labels. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25739/figures/14 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11440475/

label: robust marker scoring for labels
text: PITFALL: Manual marker annotation from single genes is error-prone because markers are shared across types (e.g. Flt1 is not EC-only, Pdgfra and Col1a1 are also in some mural/Schwann-adjacent cells, L1cam is also neuronal, Fabp7 is also in Schwann cells), so clusters can be mislabeled. CHECK: Score each cluster with the mean of z-scored (across clusters) log1p CP10K for every marker panel and assign the argmax; inspect the margin between the top two panels; check that each answer-option type (Endothelial, Fibroblast, Mural, SGC, Neuron, Macrophage) receives at least one cluster. IF FOUND: For low-margin clusters, use the more specific markers (Pecam1 over Flt1, Rgs5/Notch3 for mural, Kcnj10 for SGC vs Mag/Ncmap for Schwann) and sub-cluster if needed; map Macrophage to option F, Neuron to E and SGC to D. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular-structure/annotation/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41596-021-00534-0

label: mean of log bias / detection
text: PITFALL: The mean of log-normalized values is biased when groups differ systematically in library size (neurons have much larger total counts than non-neuronal nuclei), and the log1p pseudocount shrinks low-abundance genes differently, so group-mean comparisons of a sparse gene like Edn1 can be driven by depth and detection rate. CHECK: Alongside the mean log1p(CP10K), report for each major type the fraction of nuclei with Edn1>0, the pseudobulk CP10K (sum of counts / sum of totals) and median total_counts. IF FOUND: The task prescribes the mean of log1p CP10K across all nuclei (zeros included), so keep that as the answer; if the alternative metrics disagree on the top type, note it as a sensitivity flag rather than switching metric. Never average only over expressing nuclei. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/404962 ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/more-norm.html

label: clustering determinism
text: PITFALL: Leiden in scanpy depends on flavor (leidenalg vs igraph), random_state and the neighbors seed, and on whether PCA is run on HVGs or on scaled data, so cluster boundaries for small vascular/immune populations may differ between teams. CHECK: Fix random_state=0 in PCA, neighbors (n_neighbors=20, n_pcs=30) and leiden (resolution=0.6); rerun with another seed or with Louvain, and confirm that the major label of the top-Edn1 type and its ranking are unchanged. IF FOUND: If the ranking flips, report the instability and favor the result whose labels best match the marker evidence. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.external.pp.scanorama_integrate.html

label: raw counts need normalize/log/HVG/scale before PCA
text: PITFALL: The data file 158542059.node holds raw UMI counts (CSR, 100000 cells x 40352 genes; obs has cell_type 18 levels, donor 12, cytokine 91, treatment 2, sample 1092), and running PCA on raw or unscaled counts makes PC1 track sequencing depth rather than biology. CHECK: confirm X values are integers and correlate PC1 with obs total counts (tscp_count / log1p_total_counts). IF FOUND: use the standard pipeline first: normalize_total, log1p, highly variable genes (~2000), scale, then PCA; report which preprocessing was used. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: categorical factors must be one-hot in PC R2
text: PITFALL: Encoding a categorical factor as integer codes in a linear regression of PC1 on that factor gives a meaningless R2 that depends on label order. CHECK: make sure each factor (cell_type, donor, cytokine, treatment) enters as one-hot dummies or a one-way ANOVA (R2 = between-group SS / total SS of PC1). IF FOUND: refit with dummies; the scater getExplanatoryPCs and kBET/scib pcRegression approach is marginal R2 of each PC from a per-variable linear model with the factor as categorical. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/scater/src/R/getExplanatoryPCs.R

label: treatment nested in cytokine; use marginal R2
text: PITFALL: In this dataset 'PBS' is itself one of the 91 cytokine levels, so treatment (PBS vs cytokine) is an exact coarsening of cytokine; by OLS algebra the marginal R2 of treatment on PC1 can never exceed that of cytokine, and adding both to one model makes treatment fully aliased. CHECK: crosstab treatment x cytokine to confirm nesting. IF FOUND: compute a separate marginal (one-factor) R2 per variable rather than sequential/Type I sums of squares from one joint model, where order changes the result and nested terms get zero. SOURCE: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1365-2656.2009.01634.x

label: order dependence of joint-model variance shares
text: PITFALL: In an unbalanced design (cell type proportions differ by donor and by well), sequential Type I sums of squares from a joint model give order-dependent variance shares, and marginal R2 values can overlap and sum to more than 1. CHECK: fit PC1 ~ each factor alone and also check whether the ranking changes under Type II/partial R2 (each factor adjusted for the others). IF FOUND: report the marginal R2 ranking as primary (it matches the scater/scib convention) and note whether partial R2 agrees; if they disagree, report both instead of quietly picking one. SOURCE: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/DMAR/vignettes/sums_of_squares.html

label: many-level factor R2 inflation
text: PITFALL: A factor with many levels (cytokine, 91 levels) picks up some R2 by chance (about (k-1)/n under the null), so in small subsets it can look inflated next to factors with few levels (treatment, 2 levels). CHECK: compare plain R2 with adjusted R2 = 1-(1-R2)(n-1)/(n-k), and/or a permutation null that shuffles cytokine labels within donor. IF FOUND: rank by adjusted R2; with n=100000 cells the correction is about 0.001, so it matters only if factor R2 values are close. SOURCE: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/404567/adjusted-r2-for-regression-with-dummy-variables

label: do not batch-correct donor before PC1 R2
text: PITFALL: Running batch correction (Harmony, regressing out donor, scale with regress_out) before PCA, or using an already-integrated embedding, strips donor variance from PC1 and artificially lowers donor's rank. CHECK: verify obsm is empty (it is in the raw file) and that no correction step is applied before computing PC1. IF FOUND: compute PCA on uncorrected log-normalized, scaled HVG data; the scib PC-regression metric is defined on uncorrected-vs-corrected PCs for exactly this reason. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scib/blob/main/scib/metrics/pcr.py

label: cell-level vs pseudobulk unit of analysis
text: PITFALL: The unit of analysis changes the answer. A cell-level PCA lets cell type dominate, while a pseudobulk PCA per sample (donor x cytokine) removes cell type as a factor altogether and changes how donor and cytokine variance is attributed. CHECK: the question includes cell type as a factor, so PC1 must come from a cell-level PCA (or a pseudobulk by donor x cytokine x cell_type). IF FOUND: if anyone pseudobulks by sample only, redo the PCA at cell level; do not compare R2 across different units. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2

label: robustness of PC1 ranking to HVG/subsampling
text: PITFALL: Highly variable gene selection and subsampling choices can shift PC1, for example when mitochondrial or ribosomal genes or one dominant donor drive it, and the ranking may not hold up. CHECK: re-run the PC1 R2 ranking with a different HVG count (2000 vs 5000), with and without MT/RP genes, and on a random 50% cell subsample. IF FOUND: if the ranking flips between close factors, say the result is fragile and report the ranking from the standard default pipeline (normalize_total 1e4, log1p, 2000 HVG, scale max_value=10, PCA). SOURCE: https://nbisweden.github.io/workshop-scRNAseq-devel/labs/scanpy/scanpy_02_dimred.html

label: Ensembl var_names symbol mapping
text: PITFALL: In this h5ad (illumina_pipseeker.h5ad, 19259 nuclei x 32227 genes, samples 3M/21M1/21M2) var_names are Ensembl IDs (ENSMUSG...); marker symbols like Rgs5 or Acta2 live in var['gene_symbol'], so a naive symbol lookup silently drops genes or hits a duplicate symbol, which changes panel means. CHECK: map every panel symbol via var['gene_symbol'], print which are missing or duplicated, and confirm all 33 markers resolve (sum duplicate-symbol counts or pick the expressed ID). IF FOUND: score with the resolved gene list and report how many genes each panel actually averaged over. SOURCE: https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generated/anndata.AnnData.var_names_make_unique.html

label: Panel mean dominated by detection
text: PITFALL: A raw mean of log-normalized marker values is driven by how highly expressed and how well detected each gene is, not just by identity. One undetected gene in a 4-gene panel cuts that panel's score by ~25%, while panels with many abundant genes (e.g. Apoe/Glul, Mbp) score high everywhere. CHECK: for each cluster, print the per-gene mean and the fraction of nuclei expressing each panel gene (a cluster x gene table), not only the panel mean; look for clusters where one mural gene (e.g. Rgs5) is high and specific while the others are near zero. IF FOUND: report this as a scoring artifact; also compare with z-scored per-gene values or sc.tl.score_genes (control-gene-subtracted) and the max/specificity of single markers to see whether the assignment changes. SOURCE: https://piaso.org/tutorials/gene-set-scoring/ ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/1.9.x/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes.html

label: Nuclear detection and gene-length bias
text: PITFALL: snRNA-seq loses cytoplasmic mRNA and has a gene-length bias, because intronic/internal-priming reads favour long genes. Short, highly cytoplasmic genes (e.g. Acta2 and other contractile/structural genes) can be near zero in nuclei even in true expressing cells, while long genes look inflated. CHECK: for each panel gene, compute overall detection rate (fraction of nuclei >0) and max per-cluster mean; flag panel genes detected in <1-2% of nuclei across all clusters. Note which panels contain such near-zero genes (mural: Acta2, Pdgfrb, Notch3?). IF FOUND: treat a deflated panel mean as a technical artifact of nuclear RNA detection rather than absence of the cell type; judge identity using the detectable markers. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10984380/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.20/OSCA.advanced/single-nuclei-rna-seq-processing.html

label: Mural vs fibroblast overlap
text: PITFALL: Mural markers overlap with fibroblasts. Pdgfrb is shared by pericytes and perivascular fibroblasts, and Acta2 is mostly vSMC. The most conserved specific pericyte markers are Rgs5, Kcnj8, Abcc9, Higd1b, Ndufa4l2, Notch3 and Vtn. CHECK: in fibroblast-assigned clusters, see whether Rgs5/Kcnj8/Abcc9/Higd1b/Vtn are co-expressed with Col1a1/Dcn, or whether these sit in a separate cluster with low Col1a1/Dcn. IF FOUND: if a separate Rgs5+/Kcnj8+ cluster exists and loses on panel mean, the cause is scoring, not absorption into fibroblasts. Only call it fibroblast absorption if mural-specific genes are spread inside Col1a1-high clusters with no separate structure. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/fulltext/S0962-8924(23)00111-3 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/nature25739

label: Ambient RNA inflates panels
text: PITFALL: Ambient RNA is higher in snRNA-seq (~12% on average) and comes mostly from abundant, transcript-rich cell types (neurons in neural tissue). It raises neuron/glia panel scores in every cluster and can make annotations of small or low-UMI clusters wrong or hide them. CHECK: look at the neuron panel score (Snap25, Rbfox3) in clearly non-neuronal clusters and the background level of each panel in all clusters; compare the winning margin of small clusters. IF FOUND: compare panel scores relative to the across-cluster baseline (e.g. subtract the median cluster score per panel), or note that ambient contamination may decide close calls; CellBender/SoupX can be used if raw droplets are available. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9789184/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13533975/

label: Absent label is not absent cells
text: PITFALL: Calling a lineage absent because no cluster is assigned to it confuses 'not detected by this scoring' with 'not in the data'. Rare populations can also merge into neighbours at one Leiden resolution. CHECK: before concluding absence or depletion, count nuclei that individually express mural-specific genes (e.g. Rgs5>0 and Kcnj8 or Higd1b>0), and see whether they concentrate in one cluster. IF FOUND: if a coherent mural-like cluster exists, the zero comes from the scoring or assignment rule, not from biology, dissociation loss or resolution. A biology or resolution explanation is supported only if such nuclei are scattered or absent. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7852188/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10412410/

label: Leiden seed and default sensitivity
text: PITFALL: Exploratory Leiden results depend on the random seed and the scanpy defaults (flavor, n_pcs, n_neighbors), so cluster counts and small-cluster membership can shift between runs and nuclei counts per lineage are not exact. CHECK: rerun with 2-3 seeds or record the defaults used (sc.pp.highly_variable_genes flavor on log data, n_comps=50, n_neighbors=15, leiden res 0.8), and see whether the lineage assignments and the mural count change. IF FOUND: report the count with the parameters used and note that it is sensitive to them; the qualitative conclusion should hold across seeds. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.06.16.732539

label: Raw counts and sample structure
text: PITFALL: The data has 3 samples (3M, 21M1, 21M2; adult vs aged), and X must be raw integer counts for normalize_total(1e4)+log1p. Running on already-normalized X, or batch-driven clusters, will change clusters and panel scores. CHECK: confirm that X holds integers and that layers is empty (it is in this file); tabulate cluster x sample_id to see whether any cluster comes from a single sample. IF FOUND: if X is not counts, find the raw counts; note any sample-specific clusters but keep the specified workflow (the task does not ask for integration). SOURCE: https://piaso.org/tutorials/gene-set-scoring/

label: FINDING
text: FINDING: In split-pool combinatorial barcoding (SPLiT-seq / Parse Evercode), the round-1 barcode is the well of the first (reverse-transcription) plate, and samples are loaded into those wells, so round-1 is the sample-specific barcode and is confounded with sample identity (in this dataset, donor x cytokine). Round-2 and round-3 are ligation wells that pooled cells are randomly redistributed into, so they are essentially random with respect to sample. The sublibrary (subpool, i7 PCR index) is a random split of the pooled cells, made only to tell barcode collisions apart, so it is a technical batch that is not confounded with sample by design. Only bc1/round-1 should be treated as a proxy for sample, not as an independent batch that could add to donor variance. QUESTION: What do the round 1/2/3 barcodes and sublibrary encode, and which is confounded with sample? text: FINDING: The web gives no single prescribed null for ranking factors by PC1 R2 at the cell level. The closest authoritative guidance (the variancePartition docs) says a categorical variable with many levels fitted as a fixed effect absorbs variance even under the null and gives biased variance fractions, so all categorical factors should be fitted as random effects in one linear mixed model (ML, not REML). Treatment is nested in cytokine, so its marginal R2 cannot exceed cytokine's raw R2. The question is only whether cytokine's excess over its chance floor is real. HOW SURE: medium. The vignette calls RPCA conservative and says raising k.anchor (e.g. to 20) strengthens alignment. QUESTION: In Seurat's RPCA integration (FindIntegrationAnchors with reduction='rpca' followed by IntegrateData), what are the default k.anchor, k.weight and dims, and how do anchor weights correct the expression matrix? ANSWER: Defaults: FindIntegrationAnchors uses dims=1:30, k.anchor=5, k.filter=200, k.score=30, anchor.features=2000, l2.norm=TRUE and max.features=200. IntegrateData uses dims=1:30, k.weight=100 and sd.weight=1, and weight.reduction=NULL, so a new PCA is computed to get the weights. Before anchoring, RPCA needs a PCA run on each batch separately, using scaled shared features. It projects each dataset into the other's PCA space and keeps mutual nearest neighbours as anchors. Anchors are filtered with k.filter in the max.features space, then scored by shared-neighbour overlap with k.score; scores are clipped at the 0.01 and 0.90 quantiles and rescaled to 0-1. Correction: for each query cell, the weight of each of its k.weight nearest anchors is (1 - distance to the anchor / distance to the k.weight-th anchor) x anchor score. A Gaussian kernel with bandwidth sd.weight is applied and the weights are normalised over the k.weight anchors. The integration matrix holds the expression difference between the two cells of each anchor pair. Multiplying the weights by this matrix gives a transformation matrix, which is subtracted from the query's expression matrix. With several batches this is done pairwise in an order set by a guide tree; the distance between two datasets is the cell count of the smaller one divided by the number of anchors between them. With LogNormalize, the result is a corrected 'integrated' data assay over the anchor features. The vignette calls RPCA more conservative than CCA and says raising k.anchor (e.g. to 20) strengthens alignment. My own reading, not stated in the docs: because every cell uses its 100 nearest anchors, small populations such as endothelial and mural cells with few anchors of their own may borrow correction vectors from anchors of other cell types. HOW SURE: high. SOURCES: https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/findintegrationanchors, https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/integratedata, https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v4.3/integration_rpca.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Is Rgs5 expressed in sensory neurons of mouse dorsal root ganglia, or is it considered specific to pericytes there? ANSWER: Rgs5 is not a recognised DRG sensory-neuron gene. Mouse DRG work treats it as a pericyte/mural marker. In the Zeisel 2018 mouse nervous system atlas (mousebrain.org Rgs5 page), no DRG sensory neuron cluster (PSPEP/PSNP/PSNF etc.) expresses Rgs5 at trinarization >=0.95. The only neuronal clusters listed are weak: spinal inhibitory SCINH5 at 0.59 and sympathetic noradrenergic SYNOR3 at 0.67. By comparison, pericytes score 7-15 and arterial endothelium 24, and Rgs5 is a marker only of pericyte cluster PER1. DRG and TG scRNA-seq studies (Jager et al. 2022, Wellcome Open Res, Fig 1: 'Rgs5 = pericytes'; Mapps et al. 2022, Cell Reports: mural cells Rgs5/Vtn; TG 2023, Frontiers) use Rgs5 as the pericyte/mural marker. A Rgs5-high cluster assigned to neurons therefore points to mural nuclei (possibly with neuronal ambient signal) rather than true neuronal Rgs5. That supports the mural-dilution reading. Caveat: Rgs5 is not strictly pericyte-only, since it is also expressed in vSMCs and in arterial/capillary endothelium. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: http://mousebrain.org/genes/Rgs5.html, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35950162/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnmol.2023.1117065/full.

In the Zeisel 2018 mouse nervous system atlas (mousebrain.org Rgs5 page), no DRG sensory neuron cluster (PSPEP/PSNP/PSNF etc.) expresses Rgs5 at trinarization >=0.95. The only neuronal clusters listed are weak: spinal inhibitory SCINH5 at 0.59 and sympathetic noradrenergic SYNOR3 at 0.67. By comparison, pericytes score 7-15 and arterial endothelium 24, and Rgs5 is a marker only of pericyte cluster PER1. DRG and TG scRNA-seq studies (Jager et al. 2022, Wellcome Open Res, Fig 1: 'Rgs5 = pericytes'; Mapps et al. 2022, Cell Reports: mural cells Rgs5/Vtn; TG 2023, Frontiers) use Rgs5 as the pericyte/mural marker. A Rgs5-high cluster assigned to neurons therefore points to mural nuclei (possibly with neuronal ambient signal) rather than true neuronal Rgs5. That supports the mural-dilution reading. Caveat: Rgs5 is not strictly pericyte-only, since it is also expressed in vSMCs and in arterial/capillary endothelium. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: http://mousebrain.org/genes/Rgs5.html, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35950162/, https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnmol.2023.1117065/full.
